record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Describe all the functions f (x, y) of two variables defined in a neighbourhood of (0, 0) ∈ R2 such that • fy(0, 0) ̸≡ 0; • fy(0, 0) = 0; • fx(x - fx) - f fy is locally smooth (or, more precisely, extends up to a locall y smooth function). A more general version of this question (which would immediately clarif y the local structure of singular points for a wide class of Nijenhuis operators) is as follows.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem belongs to the program of describing singular points of two- and three-dimensional Nijenhuis operators. Related work (e.g. on two-dimensional Nijenhuis operators and on gl-regular and elementary differential singularities in dimension three) addresses neighbouring questions but does not provide a full classification of the smooth germs $f(x,y)$ characterized by the stated smoothness condition. No source found that resolves this specific classification problem; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of two-dimensional Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies singularities in 2D where the description reduces to smoothness of functions depending on partial derivatives.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related 2D classification work; does not settle the precise problem as stated.

status_evidence.title: Elementary Differential Singularities of Three-Dimensional Nijenhuis Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on differential singularities in dimension three.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the classification of singular points of Nijenhuis operators is an active, ongoing program.
